When Claude session ends, everything important disappears. Finally fixed the agent amnesia problem.
TLDR: I gave my Claude Code, Codex & OpenClaw agents a shared brain. Now they never forget a fix, a decision, or a hard-won trace again.
You know that sick feeling as an engineer.
You (or your agent) finally crack a nasty prod issue at 2 a.m. like a race condition fixed, auth edge case handled, migration script perfected, obscure traceback understood… then the session ends and it’s gone forever.
Next week you’re staring at the exact same error like it’s brand new.
I got tired of it.
So I started Hivemind, an open-source shared memory layer that connects Claude Code, Codex, and OpenClaw across sessions and across our engineering team.
It quietly captures every prompt, tool call, file operation, decision, and trace your agents already create, stores them in a virtual filesystem, and turns them into instantly searchable, living knowledge.
No more “ask Bob.” No more digging through old Slack threads Or re-learning things you already figured out.
Now I can instantly ask my agents things like:
  • “How did I fix that Postgres connection pool exhaustion last time?”
  • “What approach did we take for the auth refactor?”
  • “Have we seen this exact traceback before?”
  • “What was the reasoning behind that DB sharding decision?”
  • “What did my agent work on in yesterday’s session?”
The answers are just… there.

We’ve been running it internally for weeks.

This wasn’t some sci-fi “swarm intelligence” fantasy. It was something way more powerful:
Real coordination. Real continuity. Real team memory.
All messages stored in sessions table, all markdown wikis stored in memory table.

You already run multiple coding agents.

Modern engineering teams have massive parallelism. Code gets written, bugs get crushed, migrations ship. But the coordination model is still primitive.
Knowledge dies in the session it was born in.

What Hivemind Actually Does

It captures every trace your agents already create, stores it in a virtual filesystem, and turns it into searchable, living knowledge.
Suddenly you can ask:
  • What did I work on in my last session?
  • Have we seen this error before?
  • What approach did the team take for the auth refactor?
  • Who was on this incident earlier today?
  • Why the hell did we choose this deployment pattern?
The answers are just… there.
Open source:
https://github.com/activeloopai/hivemind

The Biggest Surprise

For me wasn’t the autonomy. It was the continuity.
My agents now act like they actually remember the project history. I can pull same-day context, see what got shipped vs blocked, and what trade-offs we made. Without anyone writing a single status update.
A simple way to think about it: Without it -> one engineer (or one agent) learns something once. With it -> the whole engineering team (and every future session) learns it once.
Our agents are finally building organizational memory, not just spitting out code.
Summary automatically generated from Claude Code session

Proof It Works

We ran a quick test with 10 agents sharing memory on an autoresearch + Karpathy's training task. They converged noticeably faster because nobody had to rebuild the same context from scratch every time. Every mistake from past 10 concurrent experiments was captured.
Single agent vs 10 concurrent agents sharing memory. As number of steps grow, converges exponentially faster.
Try it yourself:
https://github.com/activeloopai/autoresearch_deeplake_swarm

How Much Does It Cost?

It’s cheap. My whole team used it last week for $2.45. Scales to roughly $50/month company-wide.
Pretty reasonable “coordination tax” for never losing context again.
Our internal number of messages generated per day

Hivemind crushes exactly the things that slow down real engineering teams:

  • Incident memory (what happened, what was ruled out, who owns what)
  • Decision memory (architecture choices, schema changes, deployment rules)
  • Active coordination (blockers, owners, next actions)
Especially for small-to-mid teams, one unclear blocker can slow down the whole company. This fixes that.

Ready to Stop Losing Knowledge?

If you run Claude Code, the setup is literally 4 commands:
/plugin marketplace add activeloopai/hivemind"
/plugin install hivemind
/reload-plugins
/hivemind:login
OpenClaw
openclaw plugins install hivemind
Codex: Just prompt it 
Fetch and follow instructions from <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/activeloopai/hivemind/main/codex/INSTALL.md> then restart and authenticate when prompted.
First questions I asked once it was live:
  • “What did I work on in my last session?”
  • “Have we seen this error before?”
You can also create workspaces (like channels in Slack) or keep a personal org for weekend hacks. For sensitive stuff, just turn capture off and re-enable later.
If you’re a dev running multiple coding agents and constantly losing hard-won context… this might be the highest-ROI thing you install this month.
